A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, renamed from ACE to CART, with matching core methods and datasets. Text, equations, figures and tables are readable. However, v1 ends after its references despite referring to appendices containing baseline details and audio/video ablations, limiting comparison with the supplementary material supplied in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original ACE retrieval results, component ablations, configuration experiments, throughput measurements and embedding visualizations in Tables 1–5 and Figures 4–5.

after.justification: v2 reports original CART retrieval and efficiency results, with component ablations and sensitivity results in the main text and appendices, including Tables 8, 10 and 11.

M1.justification: Both retain ImageBind embeddings, K-Means plus residual quantization, collision-resolving identifier tokens, generated caption queries, coarse-to-fine fusion, consistency regularization and constrained beam search. ACE/CART, query generation/caption enhancement and ID table/prefix database are renamed descriptions; no procedural change is established.

E1.justification: Both evaluate text-to-image retrieval on Flickr30K and MS-COCO, text-to-audio retrieval on Clotho and AudioCaps, and text-to-video retrieval on MSR-VTT and MSVD. Added comparisons remain within these tasks and the existing corpus-scale throughput scenario.

E2.justification: v2 adds BLIP-2 and InternVL-G comparisons in Table 1 and GRACE with Semantic, Structured and Atomic identifiers in Table 3. Its audio comparison adds HTSAT-BERT and VALOR-B while removing ImageBind(Huge), which remains in image/video comparisons. This substantially broadens comparator coverage beyond v1's dual-tower comparisons.

E3.justification: v1 specifies quantization training with batch 2048 on one V100 and retrieval training with batch 512 on four V100s; v2 replaces this with a blanket four-V100, batch-256 statement. This establishes a reported setting revision, not verified reruns. v2 also specifies new decoder-depth/codebook-dimension sweeps and a single-tower throughput comparison using 1M candidates and 100 concurrent queries.

E4.justification: v2 supplies audio/video component ablations in Table 8 and decoder-depth and codebook-dimension sensitivity analyses in Tables 10–11. It removes v1 Table 2's constrained-beam-search ablation; the other MS-COCO ablations move to Table 9. The earlier audio/video ablations were referenced but unavailable, so their appearance establishes newly supplied evidence, not necessarily newly performed experiments.

E5.justification: Both report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, standard deviations, confidence intervals or significance tests. v2 introduces no statistical uncertainty reporting practice.

E6.justification: The audio results change substantially: reported Clotho R@1 changes from 48.44 to 46.4 and AudioCaps R@1 from 32.94 to 49.8. Several audio baseline scores also change. These are revised reports rather than established same-setting gains. v2 adds comparison and supplementary result entries and changes the three-encoder-layer R@1 from 81.84 to 81.78. Most retained image/video scores match after rounding.

T1.justification: v1 Figure 1 explicitly states O(N*M) complexity for dual-tower retrieval and O(N*Len(ID)) for generative retrieval; v2's replacement figure omits these mathematical scaling statements. The method definitions and Equations (1)–(8) remain unchanged, with no added proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: v1's abstract and introduction claim state-of-the-art performance and a 15.27% average R@1 advantage. v2 drops these headline assertions and concludes that CART balances retrieval performance and efficiency relative to single- and dual-tower frameworks. The first comprehensive generative text-to-image/audio/video retrieval claim remains.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of the single-tower accuracy/latency tradeoff, GRACE's identifier limitations and codebook-dimension effects. It removes v1's explanation that ACE is insensitive to audio duration and its limitation concerning independently trained identifier and retrieval models. Dynamic-corpus and text-only-query limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 removes v1's named caption generators—Qwen-VL, BLIP-2, Qwen-Audio, Video-LLaMA and Video-LLaVA—and its description of handcrafted diverse prompts. It also omits dropout 0.1, beam sizes 5/25/50 and the throughput experiment's beam size 5. Appendix C retains much of the quantization architecture and optimizer information, but substantial reproduction guidance and row-specific baseline provenance are lost.

R1.justification: The positioning expands from a predominantly dual-tower critique to explicit discussion of single-tower, dual-tower and generative competitors. GRACE was already cited in v1 but becomes a directly discussed rival in v2. New citations include InternVL, BLIP, Flamingo, VALOR and generative recommendation work, while substantial earlier quantization and related-method discussion is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and experimental narrative undergo extensive rewriting. Experiments gain separate comparison subsections, detailed datasets/settings/metrics move into appendices, and limitations move after the conclusion. Framework and module terminology also change throughout.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 are substantially redrawn, including single-tower retrieval and clearer architecture annotations. v2 adds comparison and supplementary tables, splits v1's image-ablation table between the main text and appendix, and removes the identifier-capacity column. Figures 4–5 retain their underlying displays within a substantially reorganized document layout.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical context through single-tower and GRACE comparisons, supplies supplementary ablations and moderates the headline superiority claim. However, it loses important caption-generation, decoding and baseline-provenance details, while substantial audio-score revisions remain unexplained. Its assertion of leading every metric also conflicts with Table 2: AudioCaps R@10 is 86.8 for CART versus 88.4 for ONE-PEACE. These material gains and losses prevent a confident net quality judgment.
